summary.value: The Red Shaver is a sex-linked laying hybrid that comes from Canada, where the Shaver line has its roots. Because of the cross, chicks can be sorted by color the day they hatch. Pullets are reddish brown with white underfeathers, while cockerels are white with a few red marks. Grown birds are light, at roughly 3 to 5 pounds. Hens are known for heavy laying, with reports of about 305 to 315 large brown eggs a year. They have a name for being quiet and calm, which makes them easy to keep in a backyard flock. Their Canadian background means they handle cold weather well. This bird suits keepers who care most about a steady supply of eggs rather than showing or breeding their own chicks.
